title: Democrats sweep Congress and key governor’s races, and Wall Street weighs what a “blue tsunami” means for the AI data-center boom
summary: Democrats won control of both the Senate and the House in Tuesday’s midterms, and won governor’s races in Texas, Ohio, and Georgia, where several winners have called for pauses on data center construction, NBC News reported. In Texas, Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Gov. Greg Abbott; Wolfe Research had flagged an Abbott loss as the one result that could plausibly spook markets, since Texas is a critical market for data centers. JPMorgan analysts warned the outcome could trigger an “AI sell-off on assumed higher regulation,” citing possible data-center restrictions and higher taxes on corporations and top earners. Stock futures slid at first on the results, then rebounded strongly early Wednesday, with Dow futures up nearly 800 points by 7:15 a.m. ET.

title: S&P 500 futures climb back from an overnight drop as investors digest the Democratic sweep
summary: U.S. stock index futures rose this morning, reversing sharp early losses after Democrats took control of both chambers of Congress, Reuters reported. Nasdaq 100 futures had fallen as much as 2.4% and S&P 500 futures as much as 1.4% overnight, but recovered after President Trump accepted the results. At 4:22 a.m. ET, S&P 500 E-minis were up 0.35%, Dow E-minis up 0.84%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis up 0.16%. Data center stocks such as IREN, Hut 8, and Applied Digital fell premarket, while solar stocks gained, with First Solar up 8.1%.

title: AMD beats estimates and says server revenue should double in 2027, and Wall Street raises its targets
summary: AMD posted third-quarter adjusted earnings of $2.09 a share on revenue of $13.38 billion, beating LSEG estimates of $1.95 and $13.09 billion, CNBC reported. CEO Lisa Su told investors the company expects server revenue to double in 2027 and its data center AI business to grow even faster than it forecast three months ago. Shares rose about 4% premarket after falling roughly 24% over the past month on worries about AI spending. Citi called AMD its top Buy-rated large-cap compute chip pick with an $800 target, and Morgan Stanley raised its target to $550 from $510 while keeping an equal weight rating.

title: Tesla and SpaceX slide premarket after Musk’s $224 million Texas bet falls short
summary: Shares of Tesla and SpaceX fell more than 4% before the bell on Wednesday after Democrats won major races in Texas, where both companies are based, Business Insider reported. James Talarico beat Ken Paxton for the U.S. Senate seat and Gina Hinojosa unseated Gov. Greg Abbott. Musk spent roughly $224 million backing Republican candidates in Texas, according to The New York Times. If the drops hold at the open, the two companies could lose more than $140 billion in combined market value; Wedbush’s Dan Ives said Musk “needs to find the path forward with Texas now.”

title: Arista Networks posts its fastest growth since its IPO, and guides higher on AI networking demand
summary: Arista Networks reported third-quarter revenue of about $3.66 billion, up 58.5% from a year earlier, its highest year-over-year growth since going public and above its own $3.3 billion guidance. Non-GAAP earnings were $1.20 a share, up from $0.77 a year ago. The networking company guided fourth-quarter revenue to $3.9 to $4.0 billion; CNBC reported the shares gained 12% after hours as that outlook topped analyst estimates. CEO Jayshree Ullal said the momentum highlights Arista’s “increased relevance for the generative and agentic AI era.”

title: Google will switch off AI for K-12 students by default, but schools that keep AI off lose Search too
summary: Google said Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators turn them on, Engadget reported. Administrators can enable the products one at a time, but Google’s education chief Chris Phillips told The New York Times that “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” so students at schools that ban AI tools will not have access to Search. The change walks back an August move that turned on some AI features in Classroom by default and drew educator backlash. Google is also bringing Guided Learning, which walks students through homework step by step instead of giving the answer, to Search in student accounts, starting with select U.S. schools this month.

title: ChatGPT hits 1.2 billion weekly users, and OpenAI says its searches are now about a fifth of Google’s
summary: ChatGPT grew from 1 billion to 1.2 billion weekly active users in the past 60 days, consumer product lead Adam Fry told Big Technology’s Alex Kantrowitz at an OpenAI dinner in New York on Monday. Fry said ChatGPT’s volume of search-like queries is now roughly one-fifth of Google’s, a figure that is OpenAI’s own estimate. He also said users create 1.5 billion images a week and that voice mode, including dictation, has 250 million weekly users. OpenAI plans to merge ChatGPT’s Chat and Work modes into one experience.

title: OpenAI brings in outside hackers for its next security sprint and quadruples bug bounties for critical flaws
summary: OpenAI said it is planning its next internal security sprint and has partnered with Cathedral, whose researchers will use OpenAI’s models alongside its teams to challenge the company’s defenses. It is also more than quadrupling rewards for critical findings in its Security Bug Bounty program. In its last sprint, OpenAI said, it dedicated 25% of its product engineers to finding and fixing weaknesses, using Codex to reproduce vulnerabilities and prepare patches. The company said “traditional cyber defenses alone are no longer sufficient” and that it has committed $1 billion in subsidized access over six months for defenders protecting essential services.

title: Tencent’s Hy4 arrives with vision and computer use for the first time, and open weights on the way
summary: Tencent released Hy4, its latest large language model, and said it plans to publish the model weights and system cards in the coming days. Hy4 adds visual understanding and computer use for the first time, with special training on professional software such as Blender and CAD. Tencent said Hy4 cut its hallucination rate to 7.2% from 12.95% in Hy4 Preview, and topped a blind finance evaluation by 213 financial professionals among open-source models, according to the company’s own testing. Pricing stays at about $0.90 per million input tokens and $2.70 per million output tokens, with 50% off on Tencent Cloud TokenHub through December 31.

title: Soniox STT v6 listens to both sides of the conversation, so voice agents stop interrupting themselves
summary: Soniox released STT v6, a speech recognition model that can take in the text a voice agent is speaking and use it as context for understanding the user’s reply. The same feature lets v6 filter the agent’s own voice out of the microphone feed while still hearing users who interrupt, which Soniox calls agent voice echo cancellation. The company says v6 is more accurate across more than 60 languages for voice typing, meeting transcription, speaker identification, and real-time translation. It comes in both real-time and asynchronous versions.

title: Anthropic’s FlashProve can mathematically prove which AI model wrote an answer, without revealing its secrets
summary: Anthropic released FlashProve, an open-source research prototype for “provable inference”: a cryptographic proof that a response came from a specific committed model, while revealing nothing about the model’s weights. Anthropic says Claude helped produce the improvements, and the team backed the key security claims with proofs in the Lean formal verification language. Tested on the 400-billion-parameter Llama 4 Maverick, a single H100 GPU generates proofs at about 110 tokens per second, and a regular CPU can check each roughly 19 MB proof in about 17 seconds. Anthropic says the work could help catch secretly swapped models or tampered servers, though it is limited for now to 1,024-token contexts.

title: Two OpenAI engineers used GPT-6 Astra to design a talking gadget, case, circuit board, and all, in under a week
summary: OpenAI said two team members used GPT-6 Astra to design a small device for talking to Codex as a side project, in under a week and without direct human edits to the design. Astra designed the enclosure, chose the electronic parts and laid out the circuit board, and wrote the firmware and software, and a contract manufacturer built a small batch of prototypes in under a month. OpenAI said the model did not always account for the factory’s production limits and tolerances, so the design still needed several rounds of review. The company also announced a research collaboration with Mazda on aerodynamics and crash-safety design.

title: Three high school seniors built a free AI startup coach, and 15,000 students in 20 countries have used it
summary: Anthony Tan, Aiden Azoy, and Mia Rubio, seniors at the Alexander W. Dreyfoos School of the Arts in West Palm Beach, Florida, launched Prodigy Pro to help young people turn an idea into a real venture, The Coastal Star reported. The AI-powered platform helps students define a problem, organize tasks and milestones, and test their assumptions, and it remembers each student’s goals so its guidance gets more specific over time. More than 15,000 students in 20 countries have used it, much of it through word of mouth. The team won $7,500 in the Mott Million Dollar Challenge, which helped keep the platform free.

title: Students in Paphos, Cyprus, design the “next version” of their city with AI, and the city hands out the prizes
summary: The municipality of Paphos awarded the winners of its “Paphos 2.0 – Young people design the next version of the city” competition on Tuesday, Cyprus Mail reported. School pupils and university students presented ideas using AI and emerging technology to improve everyday life, from environmental and water projects to cultural routes, accessibility, and traffic management. In the school category, Nature Rewards from Agios Neophytos Lyceum took first place, and in the university category, Aktina from AUB Mediterraneo University earned the competition’s top score of 86 points. The acting mayor and youth council president stressed young people’s role in shaping the city’s future.

title: A 16-year-old in Dubai spent a year building a swap-and-sell marketplace with AI tools, and it’s now a real business
summary: Khalifa Alhosani, a Grade 10 student at Bloom World Academy in Dubai, has launched Tradet, a UAE marketplace for buying, selling, and swapping second-hand items such as electronics, fashion, and gaming gear, WhichSchoolAdvisor reported. He started the project in Grade 9 through the school’s AI Pathways programme and spent almost a year building, testing, and refining it with AI-assisted development tools, including an Arabic-language version. Tradet is now a live platform and registered business, and three more students in the programme are developing startups of their own. “Seeing Tradet become a real platform after working on it for so long is something I’m really proud of,” Khalifa said.

title: Tonight and Thursday: free yoga under the oaks, then Moncus Park’s Evening Under the Oaks gala
summary: Moncus Park hosts its free Yoga in the Park session tonight from 6 to 7 p.m., part of the “Fit For All” series, and the weekly Mom Walks meet this morning at 9:30. On Thursday, November 5, the park holds An Evening Under the Oaks, its 2026 gala presented by First Horizon Bank, from 6 to 9:30 p.m., with a cocktail hour and dinner that support the park’s operations and maintenance. Parking at Moncus Park is $2 an hour Tuesday through Sunday.

title: Friday: the Pine Leaf Boys play a free Downtown Alive! at Parc Sans Souci
summary: Downtown Alive!, which Downtown Lafayette calls Acadiana’s longest-standing free concert series, features The Pine Leaf Boys on Friday, November 6, from 6 to 8:30 p.m. at Parc Sans Souci, 201 E. Vermilion Street. The Josh Mendoza Experience, a Lafayette blues-rock and R&B group, opens. The Children’s Museum of Acadiana brings hands-on STEM activities for kids, and Lost Bayou Ramblers play the after-party at Chez La Fête. Organizers ask guests to leave ice chests at home.

title: Saturday: holiday shopping starts early at the Lafayette Nutcracker Market in the Cajundome
summary: The Lafayette Nutcracker Market opens at 10 a.m. Saturday, November 7, at the Cajundome, with women’s and children’s boutique clothing, home, holiday and garden decor, gourmet foods, and jewelry from small businesses. Guests under 15 get in free, and teachers, military members, and first responders receive a free ticket by showing ID at the box office. The Cajundome’s clear bag policy applies.

title: Saturday: the Ragin’ Cajuns host South Alabama at 4 p.m.
summary: Louisiana’s football team hosts South Alabama on Saturday, November 7, at Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium, with a 4 p.m. kickoff on ESPN+, the Sun Belt Conference and ESPN announced. Single-game tickets start at $30, and $15 tickets are available in designated sections for faculty, families, and “fanatics.” Single-game parking starts at $20, and tailgate spots are also for sale at RaginCajuns.com.

title: Sunday: a free Veterans Day concert at the Heymann Center honors Acadiana’s service members
summary: The Military Order of the Purple Heart, Department of Louisiana, presents its free annual Veterans Day Concert on Sunday, November 8, from 3 to 5 p.m. at the Heymann Center, 1373 S. College Road. The Skyliners, the Lafayette Concert Band, and the All Acadiana Middle School band will perform. The concert honors the service and sacrifice of Acadiana’s active-duty military, veterans, and their families.
